plateFormula: ~6 oz cooked protein, half the container vegetables, 3/4-1 cup starch (1/2 cup on rest days or during the cut)
breakfast: Greek yogurt + frozen berries + oats, or 3 eggs + egg whites
shoppingRule: Small trips (under about $100) go to Foodland Kihei. Big trips (about $100 or more, like pantry restocks) go to Costco, which is 30 minutes out of the way.
sevenDayRule: Portion 14 meals Sunday. Fridge the Mon–Wed meals, freeze the Thu–Sun meals, and move each frozen meal to the fridge the night before.
pantry: Jasmine rice (25 lb) and rolled oats
Smoked paprika, cumin, chili powder, garlic powder, chili flakes, dried dill
Shoyu, rice vinegar, red wine vinegar, toasted sesame oil
foodSafety: Raw chicken, pork and ground meat: cook within 1–2 days or freeze the same day.
Cooked food: 3–4 days in the fridge, 2–3 months frozen. Date every bag.
Thaw in the fridge overnight, never on the counter.
Spread rice and chili out to cool; fridge within 2 hours.
Separate cutting board for raw meat.
sundayOrderOfOperations: Unpack the groceries. Split raw meat into recipe-size portions; freeze what isn't cooking today.
Preheat the oven to 425°F and start the rice cooker.
Season Protein A and put it in the oven on sheet pan 1.
Chop vegetables; roast them on sheet pans 2 and 3.
Cook Protein B on the stovetop while the oven works.
Make both sauces while everything finishes.
Cool 20 minutes, portion into containers, fridge and freezer.
Clean as you go; the session ends when the sink is empty.

weeks.title: Roasting and the thermometer
weeks.skill: Roast protein and vegetables at high heat; cook by temperature, not time.

components.make: Sheet-pan chicken thighs (olive oil, salt, pepper, smoked paprika, garlic powder), 425°F, 25–30 min.
ingredients: 3 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs (about half the Costco pack)
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with foil.
Pat the thighs dry with paper towels. Dry chicken browns; wet chicken steams.
Toss the thighs with the oil, salt, pepper, paprika and garlic powder in a large bowl.
Lay them flat on the pan in one layer with a little space between pieces.
Roast 25–30 minutes, swapping pan positions halfway if the oven is full.
Check the thickest piece with the thermometer. Pull at 175–185°F.
Rest 5 minutes, then slice.

components.make: Turkey taco meat: brown 93% lean turkey with onion, cumin, chili powder, salt, a splash of water.
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes, until soft.
Turn the heat to medium-high, add the turkey, and break it up with a spoon.
Cook 8–10 minutes, stirring now and then, until there is no pink left.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin and salt, and cook 1 minute.
Add the water and simmer 2–3 minutes, until the pan is mostly dry.
Check a thick spot with the thermometer. It should read 165°F.

components.make: Jasmine rice in the rice cooker.
ingredients: About 4 cups water, or to the 4-cup line on your cooker
steps: Rinse the rice in the cooker pot or a strainer, swirling and draining, until the water is mostly clear.
Add the water and start the cooker. If 4 cups is over your cooker's limit, cook two batches.
When it finishes, leave the lid closed for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Spread the rice on a sheet pan to cool before portioning. Get it in the fridge within 2 hours.

components.make: Pan 1 broccoli florets, pan 2 cubed sweet potato; oil and salt, 425°F, 20–30 min.
ingredients: 3 lb sweet potatoes, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Dry the broccoli well if you rinsed it.
Toss the sweet potatoes with half the oil and salt on one sheet pan, and spread them in a single layer.
Do the same with the broccoli on a second pan.
Roast the sweet potatoes 10 minutes first, then add the broccoli.
Roast both 20 minutes more, flipping once, until browned at the edges and a fork slides into the sweet potato.

components.make: Lemon-garlic yogurt (Greek yogurt, lemon juice, grated garlic, salt, dill).
steps: Stir everything together in a bowl.
Taste. Add salt if it tastes flat, or lemon if it tastes heavy.
Refrigerate. It keeps 3–4 days.

components.make: Jarred salsa plus cilantro and lime.
steps: Stir everything together.
Taste and add salt or more lime if needed.
Refrigerate. It keeps 3–4 days.

weeknightMeals: Chicken rice bowls with yogurt sauce
Turkey burrito bowls with salsa and corn tortillas
costcoList: 93% lean ground turkey (cook 2 lb, freeze rest)
Eggs (5 dozen) and liquid egg whites

weeks.title: Searing and a pan sauce
weeks.skill: Hard sear in a hot skillet, then build a sauce from the pan.

components.make: Pork tenderloin: pat dry, salt, sear all sides, finish at 425°F for 12–18 min, rest 5 min, slice.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Trim off any silvery membrane with a thin knife.
Pat the pork completely dry and salt it on all sides.
Heat the oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high until it shimmers.
Sear the pork 2–3 minutes per side, without moving it, until deep brown all over.
Move the skillet to the oven and roast 12–18 minutes. Pull at 145°F in the thickest part.
Put a towel over the handle; it stays dangerously hot. Move the pork to a board and rest 5 minutes.
Keep the browned bits in the skillet for the glaze. Slice the pork after resting.

components.make: Chicken thighs from the Week 1 freezer bag, roasted the same way.
ingredients: The Week 1 bag of thighs, thawed in the fridge (about 3 lb)
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with foil.
Pat the thighs dry with paper towels. Dry chicken browns; wet chicken steams.
Toss the thighs with the oil, salt, pepper, paprika and garlic powder in a large bowl.
Lay them flat on the pan in one layer with a little space between pieces.
Roast 25–30 minutes, swapping pan positions halfway if the oven is full.
Check the thickest piece with the thermometer. Pull at 175–185°F.
Rest 5 minutes, then slice.

components.make: Jasmine rice.
ingredients: About 4 cups water, or to the 4-cup line on your cooker
steps: Rinse the rice in the cooker pot or a strainer, swirling and draining, until the water is mostly clear.
Add the water and start the cooker. If 4 cups is over your cooker's limit, cook two batches.
When it finishes, leave the lid closed for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Spread the rice on a sheet pan to cool before portioning. Get it in the fridge within 2 hours.

components.make: Pan 1 halved Brussels sprouts, pan 2 frozen stir-fry vegetables (roasted from frozen).
ingredients: 2 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
2 lb frozen stir-fry vegetables (do not thaw)
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the sprouts with half the oil and salt, then set them cut-side down on one sheet pan.
Spread the frozen vegetables on a second pan, still frozen, and toss with the rest of the oil and salt.
Roast both 20–25 minutes, stirring the frozen vegetables once. The sprouts are done when the cut sides are deep brown.
Drain off any water from the frozen vegetables before portioning.

components.make: Soy-ginger glaze (shoyu, rice vinegar, honey, grated ginger and garlic) simmered in the pork pan.
steps: Whisk everything in a bowl while the pork roasts.
Once the pork is out, set the hot skillet over medium heat. Use a towel on the handle.
Pour in the glaze and scrape up the browned bits with a wooden spoon.
Simmer 3–5 minutes, until syrupy and coating the spoon. It thickens more as it cools.
Spoon over the sliced pork, and save the rest in a jar.

components.make: Lemon-garlic yogurt (repeat).
steps: Stir everything together in a bowl.
Taste. Add salt if it tastes flat, or lemon if it tastes heavy.
Refrigerate. It keeps 3–4 days.

midweek.title: Pan-seared salmon
midweek.task: 15 min: sear one fresh salmon fillet skin-side down 5–6 min, flip for 2. Pull at 125–130°F for moist fish (USDA lists 145°F).
midweek.buyFresh: One salmon fillet, unless you moved one from the frozen wild salmon bag to the fridge Tuesday night.
steps: If using frozen salmon, thaw it in the fridge from Tuesday night.
Pat the fillet very dry, then season both sides.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high until it shimmers.
Lay the fish skin-side down, away from you, and press gently with a spatula for 10 seconds.
Cook 5–6 minutes without moving it, until the color has climbed most of the way up the side.
Flip and cook 2 minutes. Pull at 125–130°F for moist fish, or 145°F for the USDA temperature.
Rest 2 minutes, then serve over rice.

saturdayNight: Move the Week 1 bag of frozen chicken thighs to the fridge to thaw.
notes: Freeze any tenderloin you don't cook today; Week 4 can use it.

weeks.title: One-pot cooking and seasoning by taste
weeks.skill: Build flavor in layers in one pot; adjust salt and acid by tasting.

components.make: Turkey chili: brown 2.5 lb turkey with onion and garlic; add 2 cans beans and 2 cans crushed tomatoes, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika; simmer 45 min. Finish with salt and lime.
ingredients: 2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
1 can (15 oz) kidney beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onions 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic and stir 30 seconds.
Turn the heat to medium-high, add the turkey, and break it up. Cook 8–10 minutes, until no pink remains.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, paprika and salt, and cook 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and beans. Bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer.
Simmer 45 minutes with the lid slightly open, stirring every 10–15 minutes.
Turn off the heat and squeeze in half the lime. Taste, then add salt and lime a little at a time until it tastes bright.
Divide into shallow containers to cool. Get it in the fridge within 2 hours.

components.make: Poached chicken breast: salted water to a bare simmer, heat off, lid on 15–20 min, shred.
ingredients: Cold water to cover by 1 inch
steps: Lay the chicken in a large pot in one layer, and cover with the water and salt.
Heat over medium until the water barely simmers, with small bubbles at the edge.
Turn off the heat, cover, and leave 15–20 minutes.
Check the thickest breast. It needs 165°F. If it is short, cover and give it a few more minutes.
Lift the chicken out, rest 5 minutes, and shred with two forks.
Spoon a little poaching liquid over the shredded chicken so it stays moist.

components.make: Roasted baby potatoes, halved, 425°F, 30–35 min.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the potatoes with the oil, salt and pepper on a sheet pan.
Turn them cut-side down in a single layer.
Roast 30–35 minutes, until the cut sides are golden and a fork slides in easily.

components.make: Roasted broccoli; raw cabbage slaw (cabbage, lime, salt, a little Greek yogurt).
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the broccoli with the oil and 1 tsp salt, and spread on a sheet pan.
Roast 20 minutes, flipping once, until browned at the edges.
For the slaw, toss the cabbage with the lime juice and remaining salt. Squeeze it with your hands for a minute until it softens.
Stir in the yogurt and taste for salt and lime.

components.make: Chimichurri (parsley, garlic, red wine vinegar, olive oil, chili flakes, salt).
ingredients: 1 large bunch parsley, finely chopped (about 1 1/2 cups)
steps: Stir the garlic, vinegar, chili flakes and salt together. Let it sit 5 minutes to soften the garlic.
Stir in the parsley and oil.
Taste and adjust the salt and vinegar.
Refrigerate. It keeps 3–4 days.

weeknightMeals: Shredded chicken with potatoes, broccoli and chimichurri
notes: Freeze 3–4 extra chili portions as emergency meals.
Heads-up for Week 4: the huli-huli chicken marinates Saturday night, so buy the thighs, pineapple juice and ginger before next Saturday.

weeks.title: Marinades and a first dish to show off
weeks.skill: Marinate ahead; cook one fresh dish without the recipe open.

components.make: Huli-huli-style chicken thighs, marinated Saturday night (shoyu, pineapple juice, ketchup, brown sugar, ginger, garlic); roast at 425°F, brush with boiled marinade the last 5 min.
steps: Saturday night: whisk everything except the chicken in a bowl.
Put the chicken and marinade in a large zip-top bag, press out the air, and refrigerate overnight. Keep it under 24 hours; pineapple turns chicken mushy.
Sunday: heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with foil. The sugar burns onto a bare pan.
Lift the chicken out, let the extra drip off, and lay it on the pan in one layer. Roast 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, pour the used marinade into a small saucepan. Hold it at a full rolling boil for at least 1 minute, then simmer about 5 minutes, until thick. Raw-chicken marinade must boil before it touches cooked food.
Brush the boiled marinade over the chicken with a clean brush, and roast the last 5 minutes.
Pull at 175–185°F in the thickest piece. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.

components.make: Pork tenderloin with soy-ginger glaze (from memory).
ingredients: Glaze: 1/2 cup shoyu, 1/4 cup rice vinegar, 1/4 cup honey, 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger, 3 garlic cloves, grated
steps: Try this from memory first, and only open these steps if you get stuck.
Heat the oven to 425°F. Trim off any silvery membrane with a thin knife.
Pat the pork completely dry and salt it on all sides.
Heat the oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high until it shimmers.
Sear the pork 2–3 minutes per side, without moving it, until deep brown all over.
Move the skillet to the oven and roast 12–18 minutes. Pull at 145°F in the thickest part.
Put a towel over the handle; it stays dangerously hot. Move the pork to a board and rest 5 minutes.
Keep the browned bits in the skillet for the glaze. Slice the pork after resting.
Set the hot skillet over medium heat, add the glaze ingredients, and scrape up the browned bits.
Simmer 3–5 minutes, until syrupy, then spoon over the sliced pork. Save the rest in a jar.

components.make: Jasmine rice.
ingredients: About 4 cups water, or to the 4-cup line on your cooker
steps: Rinse the rice in the cooker pot or a strainer, swirling and draining, until the water is mostly clear.
Add the water and start the cooker. If 4 cups is over your cooker's limit, cook two batches.
When it finishes, leave the lid closed for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Spread the rice on a sheet pan to cool before portioning. Get it in the fridge within 2 hours.

components.make: Roasted broccoli and Brussels sprouts; cucumber salad (rice vinegar, salt, sesame seeds).
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the broccoli and sprouts with the oil and 1 1/2 tsp salt, on two sheet pans. Set the sprouts cut-side down.
Roast 20–25 minutes, flipping the broccoli once, until browned.
For the salad, toss the cucumbers with the remaining salt and leave 10 minutes.
Drain off the liquid, then toss with the vinegar and sesame seeds.

components.make: Leftover glaze; sriracha "mayo" made with Greek yogurt.
steps: Stir the yogurt, sriracha and salt together.
Taste and add more sriracha if you want more heat.
Serve alongside the leftover glaze. Refrigerate both.

midweek.title: Ahi poke bowl
midweek.task: Cube the ahi and toss with shoyu, sesame oil, green onion, chili flakes; serve over rice with cucumber salad. Eat the same night.
midweek.buyFresh: Sashimi-grade ahi, bought today at the Foodland fish counter.
steps: Keep the ahi in the fridge until the moment you cut it.
Use a clean board and your sharpest knife. Cut the ahi into 3/4-inch cubes.
Toss gently with the shoyu, sesame oil, green onion and chili flakes.
Serve over the rice with the cucumber salad. Eat it tonight; do not save leftovers.

saturdayNight: Marinate the huli-huli chicken thighs tonight (shoyu, pineapple juice, ketchup, brown sugar, ginger, garlic). If you don't have the thighs yet, marinate right after the Sunday shop instead.
If you're using the frozen Week 2 pork tenderloin, move it to the fridge to thaw.
costcoList: Pork tenderloin (or the Week 2 frozen one)
Sashimi-grade ahi (buy Wednesday at the Foodland fish counter)
